name: Grade 8 IIIT: Representation and micro:bit Game
description: Symbols, bits, binary, bytes, decimal conversion, Scratch Link, Bluetooth, micro:bit accelerometer, axes, sensor-controlled games, testing, and presentation.

words.definition: A way of storing, showing, or communicating information.
words.example: Binary is one representation of numbers.

words.definition: A mark or character that represents information.
words.example: A letter is a symbol in a message.

words.definition: A binary digit, either 0 or 1.
words.example: A bit is the smallest binary value.

words.definition: A number system that uses only 0 and 1.
words.example: The class converted decimal numbers to binary.

words.definition: A group of eight bits.
words.example: File sizes can be measured in bytes.

words.definition: The base ten number system used in everyday counting.
words.example: The number 9 is decimal.

words.definition: Changing information from one form to another.
words.example: Binary conversion changed 5 into 101.

words.definition: A system of symbols or instructions.
words.example: Binary code represents data with bits.

words.definition: A tool that helps Scratch connect to devices such as micro:bit.
words.example: Scratch Link connected the microbit to the game.

words.definition: A wireless method used to connect nearby devices.
words.example: Bluetooth connected Scratch and the microbit.

words.definition: A small programmable computer with buttons and sensors.
words.example: The microbit controlled a Scratch game.

words.definition: A sensor that detects movement, tilt, or shake.
words.example: The accelerometer moved the sprite when tilted.

words.definition: A direction used to measure position or movement.
words.example: The x-axis changed when the microbit tilted left.

words.definition: A character or object in a Scratch project.
words.example: The sprite moved with tilt controls.

words.definition: Controlled by data from a sensor.
words.example: The game was sensor-controlled using tilt input.

words.definition: Repeated code that keeps a game running.
words.example: The game loop checked movement and scoring.

words.definition: The rule that decides when a player succeeds.
words.example: The win condition was reaching the goal sprite.

words.definition: Trying a project to check whether it works.
words.example: Peer testing found one control issue.

words.definition: An image of what is shown on a screen.
words.example: The student submitted a screenshot of the game.

words.definition: A clear demonstration and explanation of work.
words.example: The presentation explained how the microbit connected.
